title: Infecting Mosquitoes with Dirofilaria immitis and Brugia malayi
author: Michael Povelones
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb7birin

steps.title: Count microfilariae in blood sample
steps.instruction: Disperse 5 µL (or 10 µL) microfilaremic blood in a 50 µL spot of deionized or ultrapure water on a microscope slide; gently invert the source tube 10‑15 times before pipetting; immediately scan the entire drop and count all microfilariae; calculate concentration by multiplying the count by 200 (for 5 µL) or 100 (for 10 µL); perform replicate counts and average; for more diluted blood count 10 µL; larger volumes (e.g., 40 µL blood in 200 µL water) may be used if needed.

steps.title: Prepare infection dilution
steps.instruction: In a tissue‑culture hood, mix infected blood with heparinized sheep blood (Hemostat Catalog #SBH100) to obtain a final concentration of 4000‑5000 mf mL⁻¹; aliquot under sterile conditions; keep the diluted sample warm at 37 °C in a heat block or circulating water bath; verify the concentration by recounting 10 µL of the dilution in a 50 µL water drop and averaging replicate counts.

steps.title: Load feeder with warm blood
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm a 300 mL Avent Phillips baby bottle (SCF693/59) and the diluted blood to 37 °C; fill the bottle with 37 °C water, minimizing air bubbles; invert the bottle, add 3.5 mL diluted blood to the depression at the bottom, and cover with stretched Parafilm; rub the Parafilm side on a lotion‑free body area; avoid splashing water onto the feeder.

steps.title: Feed mosquitoes
steps.instruction: Gently shake the bottle, invert it, and place it (Parafilm side down) on top of a mosquito cup/cage (e.g., Large Bugdorm cage, BD4M3074); optionally perform this inside a secondary container in the incubator; exhale a warm breath into the cup before placing the feeder; feed for 15 minutes at 27 °C, 80 % relative humidity, with lights off; ensure each cup receives the same volume of blood and the same feeding time; avoid serial feeding of different groups when possible.

steps.title: Refresh feeder if needed
steps.instruction: To feed additional mosquitoes, remove the cap without touching the Parafilm side, pour out the water, keep the inverted feeder empty, give a firm shake to re‑disperse the blood, add fresh 37 °C water, replace the cap, and reposition the feeder on the mosquito cup; take care not to spill water onto the Parafilm.

steps.title: Sort blood‑fed mosquitoes
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mosquitoes with CO₂ using a Flypad (Flystuff 59‑114) and separate blood‑fed from unfed individuals with a generic size‑00 paintbrush; alternatively, sort on ice.

steps.title: Dissect gut to release blood meal
steps.instruction: Place each blood‑fed mosquito in a 50 µL drop of ultrapure or deionized water on a depression slide; tear the abdominal cuticle at the thorax‑abdomen junction with Dumont fine forceps (11251‑10); discard any damaged guts; transfer the gut to a new slide containing 50 µL ultrapure water; peel the gut away from the blood bolus and discard the gut tissue; disrupt the blood meal with the forceps and fully disperse it using a P20 pipette; multiple guts may be processed on the same slide before dispersion.

steps.title: Count microfilariae in blood meals
steps.instruction: Count all microfilariae in the entire 50 µL drop as described in step 1; repeat for at least 10 mosquitoes per experimental group and average the results.
